BiblicalUsage: I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, says the Lord to Zedekiah, and into the hand of them whose face thou fearest, and Ebed-melech is told, thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two verses are one promise read two ways: the king is given to the men he fears, and the servant is kept from the men he fears, and the difference is whose hand each man trusted.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
